title: The Reinebold Report
subtitle: "Even a broken clock wins once a season. Ask the Uncle — he finally found the daylight."
tagline: Week 4 — The Recap Nobody Asked For
author: Jeff Reinebold
lede: Pull up a chair in the film room, gang, because Week 4 flipped the script on three different storylines at once. The last unbeaten got its clock cleaned, the saddest franchise in the league finally — FINALLY — won a football game, and one team put up 75 points and called it a day. McMillan went for forty-five, Kyren went for thirty-six, and a kicker outscored half a starting lineup. Chalk's in my hand. Let's roll it.

matchups.recap: The mascot keeps feasting. Tetairoa McMillan (45.2) erased last week's egg with a monster, CeeDee Lamb (41.3) went supernova, and Brock Bowers (20.6) kept rolling at tight end — a wire-to-wire demolition even with Parker Washington (2.0) doing nothing in the flex. AllInTheTush got a strong Bijan Robinson (27.7) and Zay Flowers (25.8), but Jeremiyah Love (6.5), Josh Downs (4.6) and a stone-cold Travis Kelce (3.5) at tight end sank the ship again.
matchups.trashTalk: AllInTheTush has now dropped three straight and the flex keeps flexing on its own owner. Major Tuddy hung 174 and the mascot personally outscored your entire receiving corps — that's AllInTheLoss, part three.

matchups.recap: Stop the presses — the Uncle won a football game. Tee Higgins (26.7) out of the flex-ish spot, Chuba Hubbard (25.9), Sam LaPorta (22.4) and Jonathan Taylor (22.7) carried the long-suffering franchise to its first W, surviving a 0.0 goose egg from Rashee Rice in the starting lineup. Mauled by the Panthers got a huge Javonte Williams (31.3), Chase Brown (19.1) and Lamar Jackson (18.88), but Emeka Egbuka (3.3) left just enough on the table to come up 3.3 short.
matchups.trashTalk: Break out the party hats — Cracked Out Uncle finally cracked the win column, and he did it while STARTING a zero at receiver. Mauled by the Panthers got mauled by the one team that couldn't stop losing. The curse took a week off, folks.

matchups.recap: The crown fits again. Kyren Williams (36.7) detonated, Romeo Doubs (23.8) and Quinshon Judkins (21.6) chipped in big, and the Champ shrugged off a 1.0 from the Chiefs D/ST to climb back to 3-1. Questionable or Kicked correctly started Joe Burrow (23.72) over nobody's objection in this one-QB league and got Alvin Kamara (22.8) and Malik Nabers (23.2), but a quiet Jaxon Smith-Njigba (12.6) and a dreadful Dalton Kincaid (1.7) at tight end kept them from keeping pace.
matchups.trashTalk: Questionable or Kicked got JSN back to earth and Kincaid gave 'em a buck-seventy from the tight end spot — questionable lineup, kicked to the curb. Champ 🏆 wore the crown like he meant it this week. Uneasy no more.

matchups.recap: Bang way-above-average dropped the week-high 174.96 and finally snapped the Lambs' perfect run. Kenneth Walker III (30.9), Nico Collins (30.8) and Puka Nacua (27.7) were electric, and even a Bryce Young (21.46) special got in on it. Silence of the CeeDee Lambs had the quietest loss imaginable — Kyle Monangai (28.0) and a 20.48 from Jared Goff were nice, but Ja'Marr Chase (5.7) and Davante Adams (7.2) both whiffed in the exact week the Lambs needed them.
matchups.trashTalk: Silence of the CeeDee Lambs finally made some noise — the bad kind. The lone unbeaten gets Chase'd down and loses by thirty-six. Bang average wasn't average today; it was a buzzsaw. Perfect's over, folks.

matchups.recap: You don't need to score big if the other guy forgets to show up. Chris Olave (19.6), Jahmyr Gibbs (17.7) and DK Metcalf (16.5) were plenty as the Dream Team coasted to .500. False Hope posted a brutal 74.98 — the lowest score of the week by a country mile — as Saquon Barkley (2.0), David Montgomery (4.3), Garrett Wilson (5.7) and DJ Moore (2.7 in the flex) all cratered on the same afternoon, while Carnell Tate (21.5) sat on the bench.
matchups.trashTalk: False Hope lived all the way up to its name — 75 points, a true nominative-determinism masterpiece. Kelce's Wildest Dream Team didn't even break a sweat; it just watched the other fella no-show and took the W. Hope springs eternal; points, apparently, do not.

awards.label: Stud of the Week
awards.note: From a 3.7 dud last week to a 45-burger. Redemption arc complete.

awards.label: Workhorse Award
awards.note: Toted the rock all day and powered the Champ back to 3-1.

awards.label: Bust of the Week
awards.note: A started RB projected for 14 that gave two points in a 75-point embarrassment.

awards.label: Bench Blunder
awards.note: Started DJ Moore (2.7) in the flex and left Carnell Tate (21.5) on the bench — a legal ~19-point whiff. Didn't cost the game (lost by 43.62), just salt in the wound.

awards.label: Defensive Disaster
awards.value: Three-way 1.0 tie — Bills, Chiefs & Broncos D/ST
awards.note: Three started defenses each coughed up a lonely single point. The running goose-egg bit refuses to die.

awards.label: Surprise of the Week
awards.note: Projected for 8.3, delivered 28 for the Lambs — and they STILL lost.

momentOfWeek.text: Cracked Out Uncle winning a football game — with a 0.0 STARTED at receiver, no less. After three weeks of leaving studs on the pine and losing by half a point, the Uncle flipped the script, rode Higgins, Hubbard and LaPorta, and edged Mauled by the Panthers by 3.3. The curse didn't break so much as blink. But a win's a win, and the saddest franchise in the league finally gets to smile. Soak it in, Uncle.
momentOfWeek.attribution: — from the film room, Coach Reinebold

powerRankings.take: 174 and a mascot going for 45. The problem is now a pattern.
Week-high 174 and the slayer of the unbeaten. Not average anymore.
First loss stings, but 3-1 is 3-1. Chase can't whiff twice.
Kyren went nuclear and the crown fits again. Back in the hunt.
151 points and a loss to the Uncle? Brutal luck of the draw.
JSN cooled off and the tight end gave a buck-seventy. Fading.
Won without trying hard. Back to .500 and dreaming again.
75 points. The name wrote the recap for me this week.
HE WON A GAME. Scored 153, started a zero, and still got there.
Three straight Ls and the flex keeps betraying its owner. Snakebit.

lastWord: That's Week 4, gang. We learned the unbeaten was mortal after all, that you can score 75 and go home, and — mark your calendars — that Cracked Out Uncle is capable of winning a football game. Major Tuddy and Bang average both topped 174, the Lambs finally tasted a loss, and False Hope reminded us all what its name means. Set your lineups, start your studs, and False Hope — you could've started ten coin flips and done better. Reinebold out.
